title: Permea Label Schema
description: What the labels actually mean. The negative-set construction is a declared enum -- this is Paper 1's P3 finding made machine-readable. Task-type dispatch is additive: adding regression in 1.1 means adding an enum value and a $defs branch, not a breaking change.

task_type.$comment: EXTENSIBILITY POINT (amendment A3). permea-eval/1.0 implements binary_classification ONLY. The reserved names below are documented but not yet accepted by the enum; adding one is a MINOR version bump because widening an enum keeps every existing document valid. mRNA expression is continuous and is in Permea's charter, so regression is the first planned addition.

task.description: Task-specific label definition. Discriminated by task_type.

label_noise_estimate.description: Estimated fraction of mislabelled records, if known. null means unknown, which is honest and common.

allOf.$comment: Task dispatch. Each future task_type adds one branch here.

definition.description: The property actually measured, in words. e.g. 'experimentally observed blood-brain barrier penetration'.

evidence_type.description: Strength of evidence FOR the positive label, strongest first.

assays.description: e.g. in_vivo_brain_uptake, in_situ_perfusion. Empty is permitted but uninformative.

provenance_ref.description: Path or URI of the dataset card documenting origin.

negative_class.$comment: THE P3 FIELD. Paper 1's third finding is that a 'BBB penetration' classifier may in fact be a classifier of *which pool the sequence was drawn from*. That failure is invisible unless negative construction is declared. It is now declared.

construction.description: How the negative set was built, strongest evidence first. validated_experimental means the sequences were MEASURED and found non-penetrant. presumed_random / assumed_unlabeled mean nobody checked.

validated_fraction.description: Fraction of negatives with DIRECT experimental evidence of the property being absent. For most published benchmarks this is 0.0. Saying so is not a failure; not knowing is.

source_pool.description: Where the negatives came from. e.g. 'random protein fragments, non-BBB-related'.

matched_on.description: Covariates the negatives were matched to positives on. Required and non-empty iff construction == matched_control.

allOf.$comment: A matched control that does not say what it matched on is not a matched control.
Claiming validated_experimental with validated_fraction 0 is incoherent. Caught at schema level rather than left to a reviewer.
Assumed negatives must say what pool they came from -- that pool IS the confound.

$runtime_rules.$comment: Not JSON Schema -- documented here so the enforcement lives next to the field it enforces. Implemented in permea_core.diagnose.
$runtime_rules.PERMEA-W301: construction in {presumed_random, assumed_unlabeled} AND validated_fraction < 0.5 -> emit PERMEA-W301 and AUTO-RUN the matched-negative probe (check D3). In this regime a headline metric may be measuring pool membership rather than the biological property, and the benchmark cannot rule that out on its own.
